title: Closed-site operations under weakly etale localization
statement:
For the cartesian square obtained by a weakly etale $W\to X$ and a closed
immersion $Z\to X$, restriction to $W$ commutes with the underived closed
direct image, and the two composites of inverse images agree. These
identifications respect the unit and counit of the closed adjunction.

proof.text: Write $i:Z\to X$, $v:W\to X$, $Z_W=Z\times_XW$, $i_W:Z_W\to W$, and $v_Z:Z_W\to Z$. The slice identification identifies $v^*$ and $v_Z^*$ with restriction. For $T\to W$, the two values $(v^*i_*G)(T)$ and $(i_{W*}v_Z^*G)(T)$ are $G(Z\times_X T)$ and $G(Z_W\times_W T)$, respectively. The fiber-product universal property identifies these objects, their arrows, and their coefficient actions. Hence restriction gives a natural isomorphism $v^*i_*\cong i_{W*}v_Z^*$.

Compute inverse image using the comma-category colimit followed by sheafification in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For $T\to Z_W$, a global index is $(V\to X,\phi:T\to Z\times_XV)$. Replace it by $V_W=V\times_XW$ with the unique lift of $\phi$ using the given $T\to W$. This is a local index for $i_W$, and the projection $V_W\to V$ sends a section $s\in F(V)$ to its restriction in $F(V_W)$. Conversely a local index $(V\to W,\psi:T\to Z_W\times_WV)$ is a global index by forgetting its W-structure. These maps on colimits are inverse: the projection $V_W\to V$ is an indexing arrow identifying the original representative with its replacement; for a local V, its graph $V\to V\times_XW$ is an indexing arrow identifying the local representative with its replacement. The maps commute with arrows of T. Slice coverings are unchanged, so sheafification gives $v_Z^{-1}i^{-1}F\cong i_W^{-1}v^{-1}F$. For the constant coefficient module sheaves of the site convention, these maps send $a s$ to $a$ times the image of $s$; the module construction in the operations definition therefore gives the same isomorphism for module inverse images. This constructs the canonical pro-etale inverse-image comparison directly from the base-change functors; no etale inverse-image comparison or presentation theorem is used.

In the inverse-image colimit definition, the unit $F(V)\to(i_*i^{-1}F)(V)$ sends s to the class indexed by $(V,\mathrm{id}_{Z\times_XV})$, followed by sheafification. For the counit $i^{-1}i_*G\to G$, a representative indexed by $(V,\phi:T\to Z\times_XV)$ is $s\in G(Z\times_XV)$ and is sent to $\phi^*s\in G(T)$. The restriction maps respect indexing arrows, so this defines a presheaf map and then a sheaf map; the operations definition lifts these very maps to modules. The unit representative under step 2 is its restriction along $V\times_XW\to V$, namely the local unit representative. For the counit, the lifted map $\phi_W:T\to Z_W\times_W(V\times_XW)$ followed by projection is $\phi$, so $\phi_W^*\operatorname{pr}^*s=\phi^*s$. This equality on every representative proves equality after the colimit and sheafification. Thus both unit and counit commute with the direct-image identification of step 1 and inverse-image identification of step 2.
